note: Parameters for a 12-week dry run of the whole placement funnel over the synthetic cohort. No corpus: the connections come from config/benchmarks/synthetic-cohort/connections.json and everything that happens to them over the 12 weeks is drawn from `seed`, so the same run happens on every machine.
clockNote: Day 0 is the cohort's own meta.epoch (2026-09-01T12:00:00Z), so nothing in this suite is relative to 'today' and the funnel counts do not drift with the calendar. The daily tick is 10:00 America/New_York, inside the send window, so a text that is deferred is deferred by the CAP and not by the hour the benchmark happened to run.

probabilities.note: How the world answers, per day, per eligible connection. Tuned so the funnel reaches the day-30 and day-60 retention checkpoints inside 12 weeks while still leaving connections stalled at each stage — a simulation where everyone advances would never exercise the no-view, no-response or unanswered-retention rules. Day 90 is out of reach at 12 weeks by arithmetic, not by defect: a connection needs roughly three weeks to reach `started`, and 21 + 90 is past the end of the run. Lengthening the simulation to reach it would make every other number incomparable with the runs before it, so the coverage check requires a checkpoint's ask only where the window actually closed inside the run.

smsPreference.note: Every simulated student is consented and reachable. This suite is about SCHEDULING, not consent — the consent invariant is nudge-consent's (design section 4.5), and modelling refusals here would only make this suite's counts depend on that suite's fixture.

stuckNote: A connection that has not moved in this many simulated days, in a status that is not terminal. Counted per STUDENT, because the number a job developer acts on is 'how many of my people are stalled', not how many rows are.

expectations.note: The retention invariant, expressed as coverage rather than as a second copy of selectRetentionChecks. A connection that sat in a retention-eligible status across its checkpoint, with a full re-ask window on top, must have been asked at least once — that is the regression the retention chain already had (an unanswered day-30 text froze days 60 and 90 forever) and it is checkable from the simulation's own ledger without restating the selector's dedupe rules.
